subject: Novum demo follow-up — actionable comparison checklist & hallucination regression plan
messages:
From: Devin Rojas <devin.rojas@novum.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: qa@novum.ai
Date: 2027-08-11T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Demo today — quick recap and follow-ups

Thanks for the demo earlier, Kimberly — good walkthrough. A few follow-ups from our side so we can qualify Redwood vs the hyperscalers for a production pilot: 

- Can you run a short comparison that covers: hallucination rate on factual QA, answer alignment on multi-step reasoning, and latency at 2k token generations? We want a side-by-side against Bedrock and Vertex (we can provide access).
- We care about quantized model parity (we've seen artifacts at int8 in other infra). Please capture sample outputs and a flag if outputs diverge semantically.
- For hallucination measurement, what annotation process do you propose? We expect a manual review for ~200 QA pairs.

I've attached our sample prompt set (novum-post-demo-prompts.csv) and we can share a small labeled subset if that helps. Also curious about how Redwood's KV cache behavior will affect end-to-end latency for long chats.

Next steps: after you propose a concrete checklist and timeline, we'll confirm resources and provide a sandbox credential if needed.

—Devin
Senior Engineering Manager, Novum.ai
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Devin Rojas <devin.rojas@novum.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-08-11T16:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Demo today — quick recap and follow-ups

Thanks Devin — great to sync. Internal plan below; looping Marissa (PM) and Ben (Eval lead) to scope and run.

TL;DR proposed deliverables (target 5 business days):
- Side-by-side quality matrix (Redwood-hosted vs Bedrock vs Vertex) over your 200 prompts: hallucination_rate (manual), accuracy on factual QA, multi-step reasoning score, and qualitative samples.
- Latency profile: p50/p95 token latency at 512/1024/2048 tokens, with KV-cache enabled/disabled.
- Quantization parity check: int8 vs fp16 outputs diff summary and 10 representative failure cases.
- Regression checklist & smoke tests we will run before handing results.

Action items for Novum: provide a sandbox API key (or allow us temporary Bedrock/Vertex test credentials) and confirm if we can use the CSV you attached as-is or if you want us to anonymize any fields.

Ben — can you own the eval harness and the hallucination annotation plan? Marissa — can you own timeline and deliverable sign-off?

Proposed timeline: plan + checklist by EOD tomorrow; test run + annotation by EOD +4 business days; results review call on day +6. If that works, we'll prepare a concise checklist and start the runs.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Devin Rojas <devin.rojas@novum.ai>
Date: 2027-08-11T18:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Demo today — quick recap and follow-ups

On Wed, Aug 11, 2027 at 16:12, kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks Devin — great to sync. Internal plan below; looping Marissa (PM) and Ben (Eval lead) to scope and run.

Quick technical plan and checklist (high level):

1) Eval prompt categories (we'll sample across these from your CSV): factual QA, multi-step reasoning, extraction from long context, instruction following, and hallucination probes (contradictory context).
2) Metrics to produce:
   - factual_accuracy (micro accuracy on labeled answers)
   - reasoning_score (rubric-based, 0-2 per example)
   - hallucination_rate (percent of responses with unsupported assertions; manual annotation)
   - token_latency_p50/p95 (measured at model output level)
   - throughput (tokens/sec) and end-to-end wall-clock for 2k sequences
   - output_divergence_idx (BLEU/ROUGE-ish delta + human note for semantic breaks)
3) Regression and smoke checks:
   - deterministic seed smoke for 10 control prompts
   - KV cache integrity: repeated-turn behavior and cache warmup latency profile
   - quantization artifacts: run fp16 vs int8 on 50 control prompts, flag any semantic changes; attach diffs and sample full-response pairs
4) Annotation plan:
   - We will run 200 prompts, produce candidate responses across Redwood, Bedrock, Vertex.
   - Two annotators will independently mark hallucinations and a third adjudicator for disagreements. Expect ~3-4 hours of annotate work for 200 items.

Attachments: I pushed an internal checklist (redwood-comparison-checklist.xlsx) to the Drive folder linked below.

Sandboxing & infra: we can spin up a short-lived dedicated sandbox for Novum on Dedicated mode so results reflect production routing and KV behavior. Need the sandbox API key and any dataset privacy constraints.

Proposed immediate deliverable (EOD tomorrow): a 1-page checklist + run schedule. I'll own the harness and annotation coordination.

—Ben
Lead, Evaluation Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Devin Rojas <devin.rojas@novum.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, qa@novum.ai
Date: 2027-08-12T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Demo today — quick recap and follow-ups

Kimberly / Ben — this plan looks good. We can: 
- Provide a sandbox key for Bedrock and Vertex (temporary).
- Confirm we can share a 200-row labeled subset (we'll anonymize first).
- No new NDA needed for this pilot — our Legal okayed a short eval exchange.

Preferred window for the run: 2027-08-16 to 2027-08-18 (we'll be available for a mid-run sync). Please proceed with the checklist and schedule; we'll book the review call for 2027-08-19 in your calendar once you confirm duration.

Also: can you include a short appendix with recommended prompts to detect hallucination amplification in long dialogues? That will help our QA team.

Thanks — Devin
Senior Engineering Manager, Novum.ai
